bullets.title: Nasdaq worst month since AI cycle began; AI trade shifts from demand to financing debate
bullets.body: The NDX fell ~7% in October (worst month since the AI cycle began) with the SOX down 15.4%—the 4th worst 20-year day on 10/30. The market narrative mid-month pivoted from AI demand visibility to financing sustainability: CoreWeave CDS at 15% yield, Meta's 'hundreds of billions' capex needs, and Barclays' AI-related CDS cohort trading 76bp wide vs CDX.IG triggered an eight-session semi losing streak. By month-end, Google –18.7%, Meta –15.2%, while Tesla +12.7% and Apple +3.5%.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler cloud growth strong but earnings reactions brutal on 'expectations miss'
bullets.body: Azure +48% (guided +49-50%), Google Cloud +103%, AWS +39% YoY in 3Q—all accelerating. But buyside bogeys were much higher (AWS ~43%, GCP ~115%), and Google Search grew only +12% vs +14-15% expected. Amazon Q4 op income guided $1.5B below consensus. Google posted its largest T+1 earnings decline on record (-12.6%). Backlog builds remain enormous: AWS $578B (+$82B QoQ), Google Cloud $561B, MSFT commercial RPO $677B, all with guidance for 40%+ AWS growth through 2027-28.

bullets.title: AI financing stress: Anthropic S-1, Meta $95B raise, AVGO $63B backstop clear key overhangs
bullets.body: Anthropic filed for IPO (ticker ANT, ~$1.5-2T valuation) revealing $657B+ in compute commitments and 1,400% H1 revenue growth; adjusted operating margin swung to +19% in Q2'26. Meta raised ~$97.5B (equity + $60B ATM) with Nvidia/AMD/AVGO as cornerstone investors. Broadcom arranged a $63B SPV to backstop Anthropic chip leases. These moves partly cleared the AI capex financing overhang but did not reverse the selloff in neoclouds (CRWV, NBIS, IREN) as Musk warned debt markets were closing to AI-revenue-only entities.

bullets.title: FOMC holds at 3.75-4.00% with 10-2 dissent; December hike priced at ~75%
bullets.body: The Fed held rates unchanged with a hawkish statement; Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of a 25bp hike. Fed futures showed ~73-76% probability of a December hike. Chair Warsh acknowledged tightening financial conditions but stopped short of signaling an end to the hiking cycle. JPMorgan flagged that Warsh speaks more for himself than the committee, giving his press conference a shorter shelf life than prior chairs.

bullets.title: Systematic selling was the primary technical driver of October's tech rout
bullets.body: UBS estimated $165-220B in risk-control fund selling triggered by the vol spike, with $35B from leveraged ETFs concentrated in semiconductors ($16.8B) and QQQ ($10.1B). MS QDS flagged $28B in levered ETF selling on 10/30 alone (8th largest on record), plus $10-15B more from CTA/Vol Target/Risk Parity the following week. ETF volume hit 31% of tape on 10/30, highest since June, suggesting systematic/top-down de-risking rather than fundamental selling.

bullets.title: Intel –25% post-earnings on PC collapse and Israel fab shutdown; semis hit 4th worst day in 20 years
bullets.body: Intel's Q4 guide came in $2B below consensus as PC units are expected to decline ~12% in 2026 and ~10% in 2027 due to memory-driven pricing constraints. An explosion at Israel's Fab 28 creates a $300M Q4 revenue impact repeating in Q1. Data center/AI (DCAI) was strong at +78% YoY but was overshadowed. Multiple firms downgraded INTC; BofA cut to Neutral (PT $100 from $145), Roth to Neutral ($70 from $120). The SOXX closed below its 200dma for the first time since May 2025.

bullets.title: SNDK (SanDisk) beat-and-raise stands out: AI NAND demand sold out through end of decade
bullets.body: SNDK reported September-quarter revenue of $11.03B (+23% QoQ, +37% YoY), beating guidance range high, with gross margins of 85.1%. December-quarter guidance of $12.2-12.6B was 10+ points above Street consensus. ~50% of FY27 bits and 67% of FY28 bits are already under NBM agreements; the pipeline exceeds available supply through the end of the decade. Data center now ~50% of NAND bit demand, up from ~20% in 2020. SNDK announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov 19.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning at extreme lows; short covers dominate; systematic flows most consequential sellers
bullets.body: GS Prime: Global equities net bought for first time in a month as de-grossing accelerated with short covers outpacing long sales 1.8:1. Fundamental L/S down 3.3% MTD but TMT funds crashed 11.9% MTD. Gross leverage rose to 314% (86th percentile) but net leverage at 73.6% (10th percentile). MS QDS flagged hedge fund nets at 51% (20th 1yr percentile) with cumulative degrossing exceeding 6% of book—historically associated with sharp rebounds when buying resumes.

bullets.title: Macro: U.S. 3Q GDP beat at 3.4%; core PCE hot at 0.32% m/m; AI capex contributes 60-70bps to growth
bullets.body: Real GDP printed 3.4% q/q saar, beating 3.2% consensus, with private final domestic demand at 4.9%. Core PCE came in at 0.32% m/m; core services ex-housing at 0.37%. AI-related spending contributed an estimated 60-70bps to GDP growth, up from prior 50bps estimate, though ~90% of high-tech equipment capex is imported, so net contribution to domestic demand is closer to ~0.5pp. Nominal PCE growth running at ~6% is too strong for inflation to return to target without a productivity surge.

bullets.title: Q3 S&P 500 earnings tracking 30.2% growth, 82% beat rate; but magnitude of beats below historical norms
bullets.body: Blended 3Q S&P 500 EPS growth at 30.2% (vs 29.6% expected at quarter-end) with 82% beat rate, in line with the 1-year average. Revenue beats at 70% (below 77% 1-year average). However, aggregate EPS beat of only 1.9% above expectations compares poorly to the 13.8% 1-year average—suggesting elevated expectations complicated reactions. TECH+ sector EPS expected +48.1% vs +30.3% for S&P 500.

bullets.title: Oil +15% in October on US-Iran escalation; Brent triple-digits since early September
bullets.body: WTI rallied 15.2% in October to above $100/barrel, fourth straight monthly gain, on US-Iran military escalation risk. Brent has been in triple digits since early September; average delivered oil cost is $131 in China and $120 in Europe, well above the April 2026 peak of $116. Gulf of Oman crude flows fell to 12.5Mb/d from a 17.2Mb/d peak, confirming Hormuz disruption impact.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury yields fell 35bps in October; bonds rallied as AI/growth concerns overtook inflation
bullets.body: The 10-year yield dropped ~35bp during the month as AI/growth concerns overtook inflation fears, with the 10-year approaching 4.75-4.80% support per JPM technical analysis. JPM technical strategy noted S&P 500 breaking key support at 7500-7600, with the AI hardware theme breaking multi-month pattern support. The 2s/10s curve steepened and long-duration Treasuries rallied materially.

bullets.title: Broadening/rotation: Russell 2000 outperformed, defensives led; equal-weight S&P beat cap-weight by ~590bp in October
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 gained +0.54% in October vs S&P -0.93% and Nasdaq -5.3%. Equal-weight S&P outperformed cap-weighted by ~590bp, with 60% of constituents above their 50-day moving averages (vs 21% in late September). Energy +14.0%, Consumer Staples +11.4%, Utilities +10.1% led sectors; Communication Services -15.2%, IT -6.8% lagged. Healthcare saw strong rotation as generalists moved out of tech.

bullets.title: JPM AI quality dispersion: FCF-positive leaders (MSFT, ORCL) outperform; high-beta neoclouds face funding headwinds
bullets.body: JPMorgan flagged that the repricing in AI has concentrated in funding costs (cross-sectional dispersion) rather than broad de-risking. Quality/positive FCF US stocks are preferred over leveraged AI plays. Microsoft cleared Azure guidance with improving capex efficiency; Oracle de-risked its funding narrative by capping additional capital raises at $20B through FY30 and guiding to FCF-positive 2H FY28 with $30B+ FY29 FCF target. Negative-FCF hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN) face more intense scrutiny.

bullets.title: EM inflation: Cost-push from triple-digit oil constraining central bank flexibility globally
bullets.body: Brent crude firmly in triple digits since early September has driven headline inflation momentum higher in 19 of 35 EM Edge economies in September. Pakistan and Ukraine each hiked twice YTD; Uganda delivered a 225bp jumbo hike; Egypt surprised with a 100bp hike reversing two years of easing. The ECB is expected to hike in December and March. Euro area 3Q GDP grew 0.8% ex-Ireland; Italy headline CPI surged to 5.6% in October on regulated energy prices. JPM forecasts ECB rate at higher levels and sees risk of further tightening.

bullets.title: Global capex cycle strong: 3Q at 10.3% growth with DM accelerating; AI investment = 60-70bps of U.S. GDP
bullets.body: JPMorgan's capex nowcaster recorded 10.3% global capex growth in 3Q26, with DM accelerating to 12.4% from 10.6%. Investment goods PMI held at 53.6. Separately, AI-linked spending contributed an estimated 60-70bps of U.S. GDP growth in Q3, up from prior estimates, though the net domestic demand contribution is roughly 0.5pp given the import-heavy composition of AI hardware.

bullets.title: Post-midterm seasonals bullish: S&P 500 up 19/19 times in year following midterms; Dems favored to sweep
bullets.body: Prediction markets show Democrats favored to win the House (91%) and Senate (67%) with a sweep probability of 66%. Historically, the S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after every midterm since 1950 (19/19 occurrences, ~15% avg gain), and the Nasdaq has been positive in all 13 post-midterm windows since 1974 (avg +25.1%). Mid-December CRSP/Russell/S&P rebalances are unlikely to mechanically reduce tech weights.

bullets.title: GE Vernova and Vertiv deliver massive beats; data center power demand driving 20%+ CAGR in DC capacity
bullets.body: GEV Q3 EPS beat with orders +96% organically; raised FY26 guidance and announced a $9B Trench Group acquisition (13x '28 adj EBITDA); increased buyback from $10B to $20B. Vertiv posted 55%+ organic revenue growth with 100%+ order growth, raising 2027 revenue to $19.6B and EPS to $10.10. Morgan Stanley models global DC IT capacity reaching 316 GW by 2030 at 23% CAGR, with a 49 GW US power shortfall by 2028. EQIX named top pick; record $533M gross bookings (+35% YoY).

bullets.title: Utility sector +2% on week; AEP $100B capex plan through 2031; solar (ENPH, FSLR) sharply lower
bullets.body: The S&P Utilities Index gained +2.0% for the week as most utilities raised guidance on AI/data center demand. AEP expanded its 5-year capex plan to $100B supporting 13%+ rate base CAGR; CNP raised its 10-year capex by $4B to $70.7B. By contrast, ENPH crashed ~20% after Q4 revenue guidance of $225-255M vs $297M consensus on weak residential solar demand and tariff/BESS margin pressure. FSLR cut 2026 guidance on lower bookings with pricing inflection pushed out to 2027.

bullets.title: ECI shows wage growth slowing at 3.1% but health insurance costs surge 6.4%; labor not inflationary
bullets.body: Q3 Employment Cost Index showed total private sector compensation at +3.4% YoY (+10bps acceleration), but wage and salary growth was flat at +3.1% YoY. The acceleration was driven by health insurance benefit costs (+40bps to +6.4% YoY). Analysts noted this is not inflationary from a Fed perspective as the wage component shows gradual deceleration and productivity gains are offsetting; long-term inflation expectations remain anchored.
